messages:
alex: Heads up — hosted API p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s around 11:12 UTC. Noticed a big queue_depth spike for hosted-edge. Anyone oncall?

mira: On it. Pulling per-model / per-shard p95 now. Queue_depth tail looks like a sharp ramp, not gradual. :eyes:

sam: Linked grafana: https://grafana.company/d/hosted/p95-spike?orgId=1&panel=7 — kernel_selector logs show a flurry of kernel_switch events (fast -> aux -> fallback) around the same timestamps.

jen: Did a quick flamegraph sampling on one of the tail traces. Two things jumped out: KV cache miss storm + repeated small batch fragments causing kernel warmup thrash.

jen: Snippet from logs:
```
2026-03-18T11:12:13Z [kernel_switch] shard=10 src=fast_kernel dst=aux_kernel reason=kv_miss
2026-03-18T11:12:13Z [batch_fragment] batch_id=0x7f1 size=2 wanted=16
2026-03-18T11:12:13Z [kvcache] evict=142 miss=37 hit=2 shard=10
```

alex: ops, any noisy-tenant alerts? This looks like a spike triggered by one source.

ops-bot: noisy-tenant-detector: tenant="acme-qa" score=36x baseline start=2026-03-18T11:10:42Z action=auto-throttle attempted=YES buckets=full

mira: Confirmed — prefetch_hit_rate for shard 10 dropped from 98% -> ~40% at 11:10. Eviction rate spiked. That explains the kv_miss reason for kernel switches.

sam: Also saw batching sampler behavior change: sampler hysteresis threshold hit -> started emitting small batches (2-4) instead of filling to 16. Small batches plus kernel switching means per-request overhead is dominating.

jen: My repro locally: synthetic burst with high cold-key churn causes similar pattern: kvcache churn -> small batches -> aux kernel chosen (lower throughput) -> fallbacks and kernel thrash -> queue depth rises.

alex: Is there a recent rollout that could have nudged kernel selector behaviour?

deploy-bot: rollout: model-runtime v2.3.1 deployed 2026-03-18T11:08:05Z to hosted-edge; change: aux_kernel affinity update + selector weight tweak. No rollback yet.

sam: That aligns. So probable combo: noisy tenant causing cache misses + new selector weights making the system flip kernels more readily -> batch fragmentation -> latency tail.

jen: Proposed mitigations (hot fix):
```
# pin kernel for affected shard(s)
invctl set-kernel --shard 10 --kernel fallback_v2

# lower max_batch for edge to reduce wait for coalescer (reduces fragmentation impact)
configctl set hosted.max_batch 8 --env hosted-edge

# throttle tenant to control load
tenantctl throttle acme-qa --rate 50r/s
```

mira: Also recommend temporarily increasing kvcache size for the affected pool to reduce evictions while we triage.

alex: Can someone run the three quick actions? Throttle + pin kernel + increase cache size. If that reduces p95 within 10m we can consider reverting the rollout.

sam: Running pin now.

sam: `INVCLI: set-kernel shard=10 -> fallback_v2` — ACK.

ops-bot: tenantctl: throttled tenant=acme-qa to 50r/s — ACK.

mira: Pushing temporary kvcache bump on pool hosted-edge (cache_size +20%) — ACK.

(approx +6 minutes pass)

mira: Quick update: p95 dropped from ~1.2s -> ~160ms within ~4 minutes after actions. Queue_depth tail is much reduced. Eviction rate trending down.

alex: Good. Next steps? We should hold rollout and run a targeted canary with heavier churn to validate selector weights. Also schedule a postmortem to capture root cause and adjustments.

jen: Agreed. Postmortem checklist:
- reproduce with synthetic noisy-tenant scenario
- evaluate selector weight deltas in v2.3.1
- tune sampler hysteresis to avoid fragmentation under cache-miss bursts
- consider kvcache prefetch/backfill options for cold-key waves

sam: I'll open an ops ticket to rollback the selector tweak in v2.3.1 and create a canary job.

alex: TL;DR Action items: 1) keep acme-qa throttled 2) keep pinned fallback on affected shards until postmortem 3) hold rollout / rollback selector tweak 4) run canary + synthetic stress 5) write postmortem.

jen: I'll capture the flamegraphs and attach to the postmortem doc.

sam: assigned rollback ticket: OPS-3247.

mira: noted for dashboards: add a combined panel (kvcache_evictions + kernel_switch_rate + batch_size_distribution) so we can correlate faster.

alex: Thanks everyone. Great quick coordination. :thumbsup:
